title: opportunistic-weight-fetch-and-commit-protocol
content:
Summary:

This note defines an "opportunistic fetch + commit" protocol for model weight chunks designed to reduce cold-start latency, improve multi-tenant residency efficiency, and enable safe atomic hot-swap of model variants in the serving runtime. It is intended as a working design that can be iterated on; contains operational playbook steps, implementation notes, and open questions for review.

Motivation / Problem statement:

Current cold starts for large sharded models are driven by synchronous weight loads and checkpoint unpacking. We want to:
- Avoid blocking inference while non-critical weight segments are populated.
- Keep memory residency tight to GPU memory budgets without overloading IO.
- Provide a transactional hot-swap primitive so rollouts and fallbacks do not expose partial-model states to requests.

Goals (measurable):
- First-token latency for routed requests should not degrade by more than 10% for models using opportunistic load vs baseline eager load for <2B models; for 7B+ models reduce median cold-start by >= 3x.
- Average GPU residency per active route reduced by 15% on mixed workloads via chunk eviction and reuse.
- Provide atomic swap guarantees: any route referencing Model-V must either see all committed chunks for Model-V or none.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not prescribe new model formats beyond supporting existing safetensors/mmap paths.
- We are not changing off-host storage APIs (S3/GCS) in this iteration.

High-level design:

Core idea: split model weights into fixed-size "chunks" (e.g., 64MB target size) with metadata referencing model, shard, chunk-offset, checksum, preferred storage path, and kernel-compatibility hints. The runtime operates three cooperating subsystems:

1) Opportunistic Fetcher (OF): background IO worker that retrieves chunks from remote storage when predicted useful. It has two fetch modes: on-demand (synchronous per-request) and opportunistic (async, low-priority prefetch based on routing signals and KV cache misses).

2) Residency Manager (RM): keeps an LMDB-style metadata map (local persistent) mapping chunk -> residency state (UNFETCHED, FETCHING, RESIDENT_DEVICE, RESIDENT_HOST, EVICTED). RM enforces memory budgets, chunk priorities, and eviction policies.

3) Commit / Hot-swap Coordinator (HC): provides a two-phase commit for model variant activation. A candidate variant deploy creates a commit record containing the list of chunks and expected checksums. The HC ensures either all chunks referenced by the route id are in a committed set or the route continues to reference the previous committed set.

Chunk lifecycle (simplified):
- UNFETCHED: chunk metadata known, no local copy.
- FETCHING: OF is downloading chunk to host SSD/mmap temp.
- RESIDENT_HOST: chunk available at local filesystem (safetensors unpacked or mmap file).
- RESIDENT_DEVICE: chunk uploaded to GPU VRAM and pinned by a device buffer.
- EVICTED: chunk removed and metadata indicates eviction time.
